doc.title: Toots Thielemans — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Second day: Montreux, Brazil, Bill Evans
title: Elis Regina in Sweden and the Brasil Project
summary: A 1972 Swedish TV session with Elis Regina led to the 1990 Brazilian albums; he later received a Brazilian honor.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Yeah, in Europe. In Amsterdam and in Belgium, and in Antwerp, also. So I was in Sweden in 1972. It was the winter and snow like that at. And that was a trip… tour, I guess, by Elis Regina and their musicians. And the idea was of Swedish television, let’s do a program of, you know, and she knew about me. I mean, it was easy. And that was very funny, for instance, to see those Swedes… those Brazilians used to hot weather in winter, right. [laughs] It’s snowing [like that?]. But in two days, we did a nice little album. And that was my, so to speak, first foot in the big door. Of course, Elis Regina, for those who follow the music, know that Elis was some Billie Holiday type icon for Brazil. And then, later on, I went a couple of times to Brazil just like that, and in… when was it? You said there’s something. Well, in ’90, yes. It was ’90. Oscar Castro-Neves, the guitarist and a producer from Hollywood, Miles Goodman. They came to Brussels for a film. And the film was finished, the recording, and Oscar said, “Toots, you have so many good feelings in Brazil, you should make a record with a Brazilian.” And he starts to name the big shots. [laughs] I said, “These guys will never record just with me,” you know. And two weeks later: “Toots, we got all the guy. We got, not Gilberto, for instance, but we got Luiz Bonfa. We got… [you name them?].
And Gilberto Gil eventually became… He was one of the militant...
What then was social unrest, so to speak. They had to fight and Chico Buarque…
And Gilberto Gil were in jail even. And lately… three, four years ago, Gilberto Gil was Minister of Culture.

And they were in Brussels and they… I mean, I received a distinction. That’s because they have no parents or stuff like that [unintelligible]. [laughs] But they have Commandador de Rio Branco. That is the highest, you know… You don’t have to get up. [laughs] The highest distinction in [inaudible] medalist. So that was my [inaudible] and then… And then, I went… that was done in Rio, most of the music with all the composers and… And it’s two great albums, and they still get a lot of play in Brazil. So they [asked?], “What is Toots down there [for?]?” so… But that’s even more jet lag, right… [laughs] from Brussels. Anyway, but I love [inaudible].
